title: What is inflation and why does it happen?
excerpt: A clear guide to rising prices, purchasing power and central-bank policy.
body: Inflation describes a broad rise in the prices of goods and services over time, reducing what a unit of currency can purchase.
It can emerge from strong demand, constrained supply, rising input costs or changes in expectations and monetary conditions.
Central banks often use interest rates to influence demand and inflation, but policy works with delays and can involve difficult trade-offs for growth and employment.
